newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Canadian pulp stocks rose in Sept - sources.
newsitem.headline: Canadian pulp stocks rose in Sept - sources.

text.p: Pulp stocks held by Canadian producers rose in September, forestry industry sources told Reuters on Friday.
No official figures have yet been published, but three separate sources said the rise in Canadian stocks had been 15,000 tonnes.
At the same time, stocks in Scandinavia have fallen slightly, the sources said.

This would mean that stocks in the Nordic region and Canada combined were more or less unchanged. Stocks in the two regions account for approximately two thirds of the capacity on which the so-called "Norscan" statistics are based.
The figures will come as a disappointment to pulp producers who are dependent on falling pulp prices to gain acceptance for the price increases they have announced.
"In a phase of price increases, the downturn will have to be bigger than that, perhaps 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes if price increases are to be credible," one forestry analyst said.
